title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether integrating a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier with a bounded automated repair budget increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation compared with accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic semantic validator. Each paired intent produced one shared_initial generation and was evaluated in two conditions: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validation + ≤1 automated repair). Outcomes: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We release archived preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts and interpret results with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to network operations (NetOps) tasks such as intent→configuration translation, configuration synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment network changes, semantic correctness properties—sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation—are operationally critical and typically require deterministic checks beyond syntactic validity. A widely proposed engineering pattern pairs generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce operational risk. However, the measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends on what is held fixed (the estimand), the generator single‑shot quality, validator expressiveness, and the permitted repair budget.

We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) that isolates the deterministic rescue contributed by a validator+bounded repair when the same single LLM candidate is evaluated under two treatments. For each intent the pipeline produced exactly one shared_initial candidate using the declared generator (gpt-5-mini). Conditions compared: (a) baseline — accept the single candidate without repair; (b) guarded — deterministically validate that candidate and allow at most one automated constrained repair, followed by revalidation. The primary research question: does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that a single LLM candidate passes semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting that identical candidate without repair?

Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation that conditions on a single LLM draw per intent to bound deterministic rescue; (2) a complete archived execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the one automated repair transcript; and (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of ceiling effects, estimand conditioning, and practical implications for NetOps CI/CD policies.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and system reports document active application of LLMs to NetOps tasks and emphasize tool augmentation and validator use [1–5]. Planner‑centric and ReAct‑style frameworks enable LLMs to call external validators, simulators, or synthesizers to coordinate multi‑step NetOps workflows [2,6]. Empirical studies show that deterministic checks and generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve surface correctness relative to unconstrained generation, but reported magnitudes vary with validator coverage, task distributions, and whether evaluations permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration [3,4].

Two methodological themes motivate our design. First, prior evaluations often conflate deterministic validation benefits with resampling or iterative regeneration, making it difficult to bound rescue attributable to post‑generation checking alone [5]. Second, many public NetOps benchmarks emphasize syntactic or template correctness rather than semantically rich invariants (sequencing, reachability, policy), which reduces operational generality of evaluation claims; several recent works call for verifier‑centric benchmarks that encode sequencing and reachability properties [1,4,7]. Our experiment follows these recommendations by explicitly fixing the estimand (shared_initial) and using a deterministic validator to assess bounded rescue under a constrained repair budget.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the full confirmatory design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7). The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents after applying prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The analysis executor and hypothesis test were fixed before the main run.

Task generation and stratification. Tasks were generated deterministically into a synthetic_topology_suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high). Each task encodes: (i) natural‑language intent, (ii) initial and expected final device states, (iii) explicit sequencing constraints (must_be_down_for_fields), (iv) preserve_unspecified_state invariants, and (v) protected_interfaces. Difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count) determined stratum membership; the confirmatory run sampled 100 pairs per stratum.

Shared_initial protocol, model configuration, and validator. To isolate deterministic rescue, we used a shared_initial protocol: for each pair the pipeline produced one shared_initial candidate which was reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded conditions. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini (requested_model = "gpt-5-mini"). Semantic evaluation used a deterministic validator implementing a full_intent_constraint_validation rule that checks sequencing invariants, required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants encoded by the suite, and protected‑interface constraints. Scoring is binary: an unflagged candidate is a pass for the estimand.

Repair operator and operational constraints. The guarded pipeline allowed at most one automated repair per pair (repair budget ≤ 1). The constrained repair operator was limited to localized sequencing and insertion edits (e.g., inserting a missing 'admin down' before a VLAN/MTU change). Repairs were applied only if the validator flagged the shared_initial candidate; repaired candidates were deterministically revalidated. Repair attempts that remained flagged counted as guarded failures in the primary analysis.

Contamination controls, inclusion/exclusion, and stopping rule. The preregistration included contamination detection (negative controls, invariant checks) and prespecified exclusion rules (exclude a pair only if both pipeline calls fail due to provider/infrastructure outage). The stopping rule halted the run if >20% of attempted pairs were excluded due to dual‑call outages. For transparency, the archived run manifest and representative artifact are available in the archived bundle (see next paragraph).

Archival pointer. Complete preregistration, task manifests, model configuration, validator and repair traces, execution logs, and analysis inputs are archived with the run bundle; the archived manifest is execution/execution_manifest.json and a representative artifact SHA‑256 from the run is 2ce4c0074b64a8c9b42ee59d2ea33f4d6af25835f8f5ec42aaa0103382696b32. These artifacts enable deterministic replay of the confirmatory executor and forensic inspection of the single repair trace.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. The adapter completed the confirmatory run with completed_episode_count = 600, yielding complete_pair_count = 300 under the shared_initial protocol. Provider/audit records show hosted_model_call_event_count = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair invocation) and stage_counts indicating shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 1. Deterministic reconciliation confirmed consistent episode accounting and no dual‑call outages.

Primary outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300, i.e., baseline = 299/300 (0.9966667) and guarded = 300/300 (1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test operating on the discordant counts returned p = 1.0. The absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) equals 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval computed with seed = 1729 and B = 10000 is [0.00, 0.01]. Because discordance is minimal (m = 1), the exact test has limited sensitivity; the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute improvement to at most one percentage point in this context.

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Stratified tallies show low = 100/100 baseline and guarded, medium = 100/100 baseline and guarded, high = 99/100 baseline and 100/100 guarded. Thus the single discordant case lies in the high stratum. The solitary discordant pair invoked the permitted automated repair: validator traces attribute the initial failure to a sequencing omission (a required 'admin down' was missing), and the constrained insertion edit corrected the sequence so that the post‑repair validator reported valid == true. The repair therefore produced a deterministic rescue with one additional repair call; the repair transcript and validator before/after traces are archived for inspection.

Missingness and contamination. Contamination checks and negative controls did not flag anomalies; missingness summary reports zero failed or unscorable episodes and zero excluded pairs per preregistered rules. The low repair_stage_count (1) indicates minimal additional model‑call cost for deterministic rescue in this run.

Statistical interpretation. The confirmatory inferential outcome (p = 1.0) reflects the paucity of discordant pairs under the shared_initial estimand and the chosen synthetic suite. Exact McNemar inference depends only on n10 and n01; with n10 = 1 and n01 = 0 the two‑sided exact p equals 1.0. The paired bootstrap CI provides a complementary bound for effect size given observed data. These inferences apply strictly to: (i) the shared_initial conditioning (one LLM draw reused across conditions), (ii) the limited repair budget (≤1 constrained edit), (iii) the synthetic task distribution, and (iv) the declared generator (gpt-5-mini) and validator.
sections.discussion:
Estimand alignment and operational tradeoffs. Conditioning on a single LLM draw corresponds to operational policies that limit model calls for cost, latency, or governance reasons. Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate. Workflows that permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration change the estimand and typically increase achievable success rates by exploiting generator variance; evaluating those workflows requires separate preregistration and execution.

Ceiling effects and pilot omission. The preregistration targeted detection of a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with planned power ≈0.8 relying on a pilot to estimate discordance. The optional pilot was not executed; the main run encountered a near‑ceiling baseline (299/300) producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and therefore reduced sensitivity to detect small absolute differences. This practical outcome highlights the utility of small calibration pilots when generator performance may approach ceiling on a chosen suite.

Validator coverage, failure modes, and repair design. The observed failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, ACL semantics) were not observed at scale on this synthetic suite. The marginal utility of a guarded pipeline therefore depends on (a) the deployment distribution of failure modes and (b) validator expressiveness. Richer validators that detect reachability or complex policy semantics may increase observed rescue rates; conversely, operator policies that disallow automated edits limit guarded pipelines to detection and human escalation.

Operational cost and repair budgeting. In this run the guarded pipeline required a single repair invocation for 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), indicating low marginal extra model‑call cost for bounded deterministic rescue under the chosen edit operator. Larger or iterative repair budgets and more powerful edit operators would change both rescue opportunities and operational cost and must be evaluated under a separate estimand.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered paired study conditioning on a single shared_initial LLM draw per intent, a deterministic validator plus at most one constrained automated repair rescued a single sequencing omission out of 300 pairs (baseline 299/300, guarded 300/300). The absolute paired improvement was 0.00333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI [0.00,0.01]). The near‑ceiling baseline limited inferential sensitivity under the shared_initial estimand. These results show that bounded deterministic repair can produce low‑cost deterministic rescue for isolated hard examples in this synthetic suite, but practical benefit in other deployment regimes depends on estimator conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and task distribution. Full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts (including the repaired episode trace) are archived to support reproducibility and targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning or repair budgets.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated by the preregistered deterministic task generator; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase validator marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended for discordance estimation and power calibration was not run; no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
